plugins.name: accomplishments
plugins.description: Teaches Claude to build the evidence record a performance review needs before the evidence is gone — a session hook that distils each transcript into a redacted digest of your own prompts before Claude Code's 30-day purge deletes it, keeping the decisions and discarding the tool output where the secrets live; a sweep that reconciles git, PR, and review history against the journal and interviews the gaps; and authoring that turns dated entries into a review, a promotion case, or resume bullets without inventing a number

plugins.name: agentic-qa
plugins.description: Interactive, human-in-the-loop QA walkthroughs of finished functionality — drives a browser, an API, and a CLI against a ticket's acceptance criteria and its merged PR, with an adversarial critic pass on both the behavior spec and the step plan, live drafter/critic pairing, and a report with embedded screenshots. Not automated test-code authoring; that's what the testing plugin is for

plugins.name: ddd
plugins.description: Domain-driven design guidance for C# applications — aggregates, value objects, domain events, bounded contexts, and module structure

plugins.name: editing
plugins.description: Teaches Claude to edit its own prose — the catalog of tells that mark machine-written text, the clarity moves that rebuild a sentence around its real subject and verb, and the never-invent rules that keep an edit from becoming a rewrite, with a command that runs an edit pass over a draft and an agent that reads a finished document cold

plugins.name: git-workflow
plugins.description: Teaches Claude to treat version control as a deliverable — atomic conventional commits split from a working tree, branch history made legible without interactive rebase, and pull requests that describe the change rather than the diff, with hooks that route version-control requests to it and block the irreversible mistakes

plugins.name: graphql
plugins.description: GraphQL API design guidance and .NET implementation patterns for HotChocolate and GraphQL.NET — schema design, operations, Relay conventions, and performance

plugins.name: mediatr
plugins.description: MediatR guidance for in-process messaging in .NET — requests, notifications, pipeline behaviors, registration, and testing

plugins.name: refactoring
plugins.description: Teaches Claude to spot code smells (classic, architectural, and test smells) and apply disciplined, behavior-preserving refactoring

plugins.name: testing
plugins.description: Teaches Claude to write, review, and audit tests worth having — behavior-focused design, disciplined test doubles, browser and component testing, a plan-gated pipeline that turns a ticket or PR into tests of the described behavior, a check on whether pushed code still matches the description that specified it, and a repo-scale map of where test protection is weakest
